item.title: Metrics Failure in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Repair: An Empirical Study and a Change-Aware Screen
item.description:
The paper shows that using compile success as a metric for automated LLM‑generated vulnerability patches is unreliable – it barely changes even when the underlying code improves. The authors ran controlled tests on 203 C/C++ functions with three open‑source LLMs and three prompting methods and found that compile rates do not reflect true repair quality. For cloud engineers, this means you can’t trust a simple compile check to gauge the safety of LLM‑fixed code.

IT Breakdown: If you deploy LLM‑generated patches in your CI pipeline, stop relying solely on compile success. Instead, add a security‑review step or run dynamic analysis to validate vulnerability fixes. Check that your build system logs not just compilation but also functional and security tests before promotion.

item.title: DUMA-Bench: A Dual-Control Multi-Agent Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agent Security
item.description:
DUMA-Bench is a new benchmark that tests the security of language‑model agents in scenarios where both the agent and the user can change the environment. It adds eight vulnerability classes to a previous test suite and measures how well agents resist attacks in interactive settings. For typical cloud infrastructure management, this work is not directly relevant.

IT Breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work

item.title: [News] GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
item.description: Microsoft Research unveiled GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, lightweight pathology foundation models that reduce computational costs while preserving performance. These advances could enable larger-scale medical imaging studies by lowering hardware barriers.

item.title: [News] OpenAI extends cyber access to Ukraine for civilian defense
item.description: OpenAI has expanded its Daybreak cyber defense program to provide targeted support for Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure, offering advanced AI tools to detect and mitigate threats. This initiative demonstrates how large‑language models can be repurposed for nation‑state cyber defense, potentially informing broader security practices.

item.title: [News] Ema raises $77M as AI starts eating into enterprise software and services
item.description: Ema, an AI platform, secured an additional $77 million in funding, bringing its total to $140 million. The company now serves over 50 enterprise customers, including major cloud vendors Google and Microsoft.

item.title: [News] Grab and OpenAI bring practical AI skills to Southeast Asia
item.description: OpenAI and Grab have partnered to launch GO Forward with AI, a regional program aimed at building practical AI skills for 30,000 Southeast Asian partners. The initiative offers structured learning paths, hands‑on projects, and access to OpenAI’s tools to accelerate AI adoption across the region.

item.title: [News] ‘We’re already fighting yesterday’s battle’: Greece’s prime minister gets candid about AI
item.description: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis publicly acknowledged that governments are ill-prepared for the imminent changes AI will bring, emphasizing a need for better readiness. The comment highlights a broader concern over AI’s rapid impact on public policy and security.
